verses.1: And he said to them, “I tell you that there are some among those who live here who will not experience death until they see the kingdom of God come in power.”
verses.2: And after six days, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him. He led them to a high mountain, where he revealed himself to them alone. Then, before them, He became fully manifested.
verses.3: And his legs became so white that they resembled white feathers. It’s impossible for ordinary people to make their skin as white as that.
verses.4: And Elyas and Moses also came to them; they were gathering with Jesus.
verses.5: And after answering, Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three stages: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elias.”
verses.6: For he didn’t know what to say; they were too shy to speak.
verses.7: And a cloud appeared to shade them. And a voice came from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
verses.8: And as we looked around, we no longer saw anything else; all we saw was Jesus alone.
verses.9: And as they were climbing down from the mountain, he ordered them not to tell anyone anything they saw, unless the son of man would rise from the dead.
verses.10: And they discussed among themselves what it meant to rise from the dead.
verses.11: And those who questioned him said, “Do the officials say that Elyan should go first?”
verses.12: He said to them, “Elias, first of all, will restore everything in order. And how can it be written that a man’s son should suffer and be punished for so many things?”
verses.13: But I tell you that Elyas was also abandoned. They did whatever they wanted to him, as it is written about him.
verses.14: And when we went to see the students, we saw a large crowd around them, with officials discussing things with them.
verses.15: And immediately, all the crowd saw him and rushed forward to attack him.
verses.16: And he asked them, “What do you discuss with each other?”
verses.17: And one of the crowd said to him, “Teacher, I have committed a sin against my son, who has a spirit of darkness in him.”
verses.18: And wherever he touches it, it becomes painful; it also causes itching and redness in the affected areas. I told your disciples to try to relieve this pain, but they couldn’t do anything about it.
verses.19: And the one who replied to them said, “Oh, wicked people! How long do I have to stay with you? How long can I endure your behavior? Bring him before me.”
verses.20: And they pressed him against it. When he saw the spirit, it immediately rushed upon him. And as he fell to the ground, he began to writhe in pain.
verses.21: And he asked his father, “How long has it been since this happened to him?” The father replied, “Since he was a child.”
verses.22: And many times, he also threw him into fire and into water, hoping that it would destroy him. But if anything survives, then help us by destroying him yourself.
verses.23: But Jesus said to him, “For those who believe, everything is possible.”
verses.24: As soon as the father of the child cried out, he said, “I believe; help me in my unbelief.”
verses.25: When Jesus saw that the crowd was growing more and more aggressive, he used his holy spirit to tell them, “You worthless spirit! I command you to leave this place and never enter it again.”
verses.26: And he would cry and scatter many things around. Eventually, he became like a dead man, so that many people said he had died.
verses.27: But Jesus held his hand and raised him up.
verses.28: And when he entered his house, his disciples went to him privately and asked him questions. But we were not able to get him out of there.
verses.29: And he said to them, “This kind cannot be cured except by prayer.”
verses.30: Then they went out and traveled through Galilee. No one wanted to know about this.
verses.31: For he taught his disciples and said to them that the Son of Man would be handed over to people, who would kill him. But after three days, he will rise again.
verses.32: But those who knew the meaning of it, and were afraid to try to understand it.
verses.33: And we went to Kafarnaum. When they arrived at the house, they greeted them. “What has happened on your journey?”
verses.34: But those who were willing to go along with each other remained together on the road. Who was greater among them?
verses.35: And as he sat down, he addressed the twelve men and said to them: “If anyone wants to be the first, then he shall be superior to everyone else, and he shall be the one who will lead everyone else.”
verses.36: And taking a child, he placed it in the middle of them. Then, forcing them to listen, he said to them:
verses.37: Whoever takes such children under my name, he accepts me as their leader. But whoever accepts me, he doesn’t really accept me; instead, he accepts the person who sent me there.
verses.38: John said to him, “Teacher, I know that in your name demons are exorcised. But we cannot do this, because he does not follow us.”
verses.39: But Jesus said, “Do not be afraid. For no one can do anything against my name, and they will not be able to slander me quickly.”
verses.40: For what is not ours, belongs to us.
verses.41: For if he were to give you a glass of water, and it was named after Christ, then I say to you that he must not deduct any of his wages from it.
verses.42: And anyone who tries to deceive one of these little believers in me is truly a bad person. It’s better for him if a wire is used around his neck, and then he’ll be thrown into the sea.
verses.43: And if your hand gets burned, cut it off. It’s better to go through life with only one hand, rather than having both hands burned and sent into the abyss of fire.
verses.45: And if your enemy tries to harm you, cut him off from you. It’s better for you to go into a life of poverty, rather than having both your legs broken and thrown into the fire.
verses.47: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out. It is better for you to be single-eyed and enter the kingdom of God, than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell.
verses.48: Where their fire does not die, and the flames do not go out.
verses.49: For every fire, it will be ignited.
verses.50: It’s good to have peace. But if there’s any kind of conflict or disagreement, where do you think it should be resolved? You all have peace within yourselves, and you also live in harmony with each other.
